hints: Picture what cooling does to molecular energies, do molecules spread out more or crowd together at lower energies?
Remember a lower temperature shifts the peak to the left to a smaller energy value and makes the curve narrower and taller.
Since the total number of molecules is unchanged, think about what must happen to the peak height if the same area is squeezed into a narrower shape.
walkthrough:
**Recall what the Boltzmann curve shows**

Think of the x-axis as energy and the y-axis as number of molecules with that energy. The peak is the most probable energy, and the total area under the curve equals the total number of molecules.

$$ \text{area under curve} \propto \text{total number of molecules} $$

**Apply the effect of decreasing temperature**

Cooling gives molecules less average kinetic energy. So the whole distribution shifts left toward lower energy, and the spread gets smaller because fewer molecules can reach high energies.

**Link shape to peak height**

The number of molecules has not changed, so the area must stay the same. A narrower curve shifted left must become taller at the top to keep the same area. That means more molecules now share the (new, lower) most probable energy.

options.A: Incorrect. The most probable energy (the x-value of the peak) moves to the left to a lower value when temperature decreases, it does not stay the same.
options.B: Correct. With less spread of energies at lower temperature, more molecules cluster around the most probable value, so the peak gets higher to keep the total area constant.
options.C: Incorrect. Area represents total number of molecules present. Since the question states the number of molecules is unchanged, the area must stay the same, not decrease.
options.D: Incorrect. Cooling sharply reduces the fraction of molecules with enough energy to be in the high energy tail, so the number at the very high energy end decreases, it does not stay the same.
